title: personal-kpi-weekly-checkin-ethan-morales-2026-03-30
content:
Week of 2026-03-30 weekly check-in (notes to self)

Context: working on continuous batching + KV prefix cache improvements for serving-runtime. Goal is to reduce p95/p99 generation latency for small-chat requests while keeping unit token cost neutral or better. Also tracking personal OKR progress for Q2.

OKR summary (personal)
- Objective: Improve production latency and cost efficiency for small-chat workloads (PLG cohort).
  - KR1: Reduce p99 latency for 8-64 token responses on g4dn from 420ms -> <= 320ms by end of Q2. (current: 405ms, target delta: -85ms)
  - KR2: Improve KV cache hit-rate for repeated-prefix requests from 12% -> 35%. (current: 18%)
  - KR3: Reduce average token cost for chat endpoints by 15% via batching/quantization profiles. (current baseline: $0.0021/token)
  - KR4: Ship canary for continuous batching + fallback policy to model-variant (quantized) with monitoring and rollback.

This week accomplishments
- Benchmarked continuous-batching algorithm with synthetic mix (50% small chat, 30% long-form). Results: 12% throughput uplift at 100 concurrent users, slight 8ms increase median latency but p99 improved for small chats.
- Landed initial PR for KV cache read-path micro-optimizations: PR #482 (still needs perf test CI).
- Wrote spec for cache eviction policy tuned for mixed-length sessions (notes attached in Confluence).
- Ran shadow canary in staging against hosted-api replica. Observed cache hit-rate bump from 18% -> 24% for repeated prefixes.

Blockers / open questions
- CI perf tests flaky around GPU contention on our test harness (seen noisy p99s). Need infra help from SRE to stabilize test harness. Filed JIRA-INF-1345.
- Quantized model variant shows slight hallucination increase on edge prompt set used by UX team; need to sync with Research to validate eval threshold.
- Autoscaler policy for Dedicated bursts interacts weirdly with batching window setting; possible policy change needed to avoid oscillation.

Next week plan / TODOs
- Finish perf CI stabilization: pair with Hunter Ellis (SRE) to root cause noisy p99s. (owner: Ethan)
- Add more realistic user-behavior traces to staging workload generator to validate p99 under tail traffic. (owner: Ethan/Maya)
- Finalize eviction policy and land follow-up PR with tests (target: 2026-04-06).
- Start canary for continuous batching + model-variant fallback in production on a 10% traffic slice. Prepare rollback runbook and alert thresholds. (owner: Ethan/Jordan)
- Coordinate with Research to run targeted evals on quantized variant and produce bias/regression report.

Personal retro (brief)
- Wins: moved PRs forward despite noisy CI; better isolation of staging workload needed which helped reproduce an elusive perf regression.
- Could've-done-better: spent too long on micro-optimizations that gave diminishing returns; need to lean into experiments (larger batching policy changes) earlier.
- Action: block calendar for uninterrupted deep work 3x/week to finish benchmark analysis and spec writing.

Notes to self / quick ideas
- Try dynamic batching window that shrinks when queue builds, expands when idle. Simulate with Poisson arrivals.
- Add an A/B in canary to compare fallback-to-quantized vs fallback-to-lower-latency-hosted-model for user-perceived latency.
- Document rollback triggers: >5% user-facing error rate OR >20% increase in hallucination/regression metric on canary eval set.

Links / refs
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/kv-cache-optimizations
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/482
- JIRA: JIRA-INF-1345

End of note.
